description: Severity tier order for the kookr issue-batch selectors. Read by the selection step of implement-github-issue.md and parallel-issue-batch.md so a blank-shape scan proposes prod-bug/outage issues before idea/micro-hardening issues, instead of treating them as peers. Ranking only — no issue is closed, edited, or hidden (auto-close of stale ideas stays human-gated).
rationale: Issue #1658: the harness has emission/flow control (drain-coupled budget, backpressure slot reservation) but no admission ranking. A 2026-07-28 window on a downstream repo admitted ~28 idea-scout issues alongside 5 auto-triage prod bugs (one a live capability outage) yet merged only 1 PR — emission control throttles arrival but does not rank admission, so real outages sat as peers of cosmetic ideas. The triage/severity labels already existed; nothing consumed them for scheduling. This file is the label vocabulary the selector ranks by: fastLaneLabels promote prod bugs/outages to the front (most-severe label first), deferLabels push idea/micro-hardening to the back; everything else keeps its middle order. A fast-lane label always wins over a defer label so a prod bug that is also tagged an idea is not buried.
gateReference: This severity ordering is orthogonal to backlog-drain-order.json (#1568), which defers invariant-gate issues for safety. Compose them safety-first: apply the drain-tier gated deferral first, then this severity ordering among the remaining safe/eligible set.
howToJoinATier: Fast lane: add a fast-lane label to the issue (e.g. gh issue edit <n> --add-label prod-bug) and, to add a NEW severity label to the vocabulary, append it to fastLaneLabels at the position matching its severity (earlier = more severe, proposed first). Defer: add a defer label (e.g. idea-scout) to the issue; add a new idea/micro-hardening label to deferLabels. Membership is label-driven so an issue joins a tier with a single label, no code change. A label must not appear in both fastLaneLabels and deferLabels.
